requirements.title: Procedure interfaces are specified by procedure statements and specification statements in definitions, interface bodies, or both
requirements.definition: The interface for an internal, external, module, or dummy procedure is specified by FUNCTION, SUBROUTINE, or ENTRY statements and by specification statements for dummy arguments and function results; these statements may appear in the procedure definition, in an interface body, or both.

pending.entry-statement-specifies-interface: After ENTRY rules are registered, define ENTRY alternate(x) with integer dummy x assigning 42; call alternate with actual -20 and expect 42.
pending.interface-statements-in-procedure-defini: Use declarations inside the procedure definition of subroutine set_answer(x) to specify integer x; actual starts -20 and expects 42.

requirements.title: ENTRY statements shall not appear in interface bodies
requirements.definition: An ENTRY statement is not permitted to appear in an interface body.

pending.entry-statement-in-interface-body-prohib: Positive source-control uses an interface body with only a FUNCTION statement, integer specification, and END FUNCTION, then calls a matching function returning 42. A companion adding ENTRY inside the interface body is nonconforming; no processor diagnostic is required by this unnumbered rule.
